title: Will this summer's climate disasters push French politicians and citizens to act?
subhead: Heatwaves, wildfires and droughts, all intensified by climate change, do not lead to shifts in public attitudes without strong political will. Still, a sense of a need for protection and concrete measures is emerging.

Finland's strategic reserves model sets an example for Europe in crisis preparedness
subhead: Distributed across the country, Finland's reserves – along its 1,340 kilometers of border with Russia – cover nine months of grain consumption and five months of its oil and gas needs. The system has emerged as a potential model for the European Union.

title: Israeli army says struck Hamas commander in Gaza hospital compound
subhead: The military said the commander 'was hiding within the compound' of Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in the central city of Deir al-Balah, but was unable to immediately confirm if he had been killed. Gaza's civil defense agency, which operates as a rescue force under Hamas, said four people died in other strikes across the territory on Saturday.

subhead: In the Alps, the Pyrénées and the Massif Central, initial figures from tourism industry professionals show a slight overall rise in visitor numbers.

title: Navigating the Suez Canal demands technical skills costing hundreds of thousands of dollars
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (5/6). The waterway connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea is a vital artery for global trade. To travel through it, vessels must comply with strict regulations and pay transit fees that can reach nearly $1 million.

title: France's cheese producers worry after summer of heatwaves: 'If this happens again next year, it will be a disaster'
subhead: Heatwaves have taken a heavy toll on milk production, while scorched pastures have forced farmers to draw on feed reserves normally kept for winter. Producers of many protected-origin cheeses can no longer comply with the rules set out in their official specifications and are concerned about the future.

title: Israel's dashed ambitions to topple the Iranian regime
subhead: The Israeli government thought it could take advantage of the war launched with the US on February 28 to bring down the Islamic Republic. But the Mossad intelligence agency's plans to enlist the help of Kurdish opposition groups and former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad failed.
